newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha edges up, near-term spreads firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha edges up, near-term spreads firmer.

text.p: Naphtha prices were a notch firmer in Tokyo afternoon trade on Monday due to healthy fundamentals as well as Friday's crude gains, traders said.
Bids for second-half May open-spec naphtha were indicated at $225.00 per tonne, while offers were assessed $1.00 higher than bidding levels. It was quoted at $223.50/224.50 on Friday.
First-half of the month was quoted at about $227.50/229.00. It was rumoured to have been traded at $224.00 on Friday.
The backwardation in near-term naphtha spreads steepened, with second half April/second-half May assessed at around plus $6.50/7.50, compared with $5.50/6.50 late last week.

In the wet market, a Japanese petrochemical firm affiliated with a major refiner said it bought a second-half April cargo to be delivered to Kawasaki, near Tokyo. The price was rumoured to be about $5.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes.

A trader at a South Korean petrochemical firm, whose ethylene plant is scheduled to be closed for 50-day maintenance checks from April 15, said it may buy second-half April delivery cargoes despite the planned closure as the firm's other plant will be up and running.
